questions.q: What makes a linchpin so valuable to a business?
a: They give their work everything and consistently over-deliver
They follow instructions more reliably than anyone else
They have worked at the company longer than others
They keep their knowledge away from coworkers
questions.why: The first lesson says linchpins pour heart and soul into their work, solve problems they notice and always over-deliver.

questions.q: Why are there so few linchpins, according to Godin?
a: Most people are conditioned by fear to play it safe
Most jobs simply do not reward extra effort
Companies prefer predictable specialists
Training programs discourage creative thinking
questions.why: The second lesson says we are taught from childhood to follow rules and blend in, so fear keeps most people cautious.

a: They feel it and choose to act anyway
They wait until the feeling disappears
They avoid assignments that feel risky
They hide their doubts from colleagues
questions.why: Godin says linchpins feel fear as well, but they deliberately choose to move ahead anyway.

questions.q: What does Godin mean by a genuine gift?
a: Giving away your best work with nothing expected back
Sending free samples to attract new customers
Offering a discount in exchange for an online review
Sharing useful advice only with paying clients
questions.why: The third lesson says a genuine gift means giving away your best work for free, with no expectations attached.

questions.q: Which example shows the payoff of giving work away for free?
a: Gary Vaynerchuk shares his best advice and gets paid work
A friendly barista brings in more customers than three others
A chef leaves and the restaurant has to close
A top salesperson joins a competing dealership
questions.why: The summary says Gary gives his best advice away publicly, which leads people to pay whatever he asks to keep him around.
